amoebae can be cultured on a fish cell line, and that this cell line is useful for studying amoeba growth and pathogenicity in vitro.

amoebae proliferate and grow rapidly in a gill-derived rainbow trout epithelial cell line, causing visible focal lesions in the monolayer within 24 h and rapidly proliferating and spreading to destroy the pavement-like cells within the next 48-72 hours.
the RTgill-WI cell line is a suitable model to grow large numbers of amoeba cells in vitro, and to investigate host-pathogen interactions.
